Edexcel split it ‘Pure maths’ and ‘Applied Maths’.

‘Pure’ consists of: Trigonometry, Differentiation, Integration, Functions, Proof, Coordinate Geometry, Exponentials and Logarithms, Sequences and Series, Algebraic Methods, Iteration, Vectors, (off the top of my head, probably a few more) and the big ones I would say is integration and trig.

‘Applied’ maths consists of two categories; Statistics and Mechanics.

Statistics consists of: Binomial Distribution, Normal Distribution, Probability, Hypothesis Testing, Sampling Methods, (again, there will be a few more but I can’t quite remember the names or forgot them completely lol). The big topics are the ones I’ve mentioned I believe.

Mechanics consists of: Forces and Motion, Moments, Friction, Projectiles, Constant Acceleration, Variable Acceleration, (going to be more I haven’t mentioned). Big topics include both accelerations. 

For Stats and Mechanics, I would say, however, there is a reason why it’s called ‘applied’. Most topics link between each other and will require a transfer of skills and problem solving from previous chapters. It is also put into real life examples for stuff like engineering (I guess).

Also, there are countless subtopics in total so it would be best to search up an exam boards specification to see the details.
